newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mudanjiang Petrol '96 net rises 43 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mudanjiang Petrol '96 net rises 43 pct.

text.p: Mudanjiang Petro-Chemical Co Ltd said on Tuesday its net profit rose 42.6 percent to 46.9 million yuan in 1996, compared with 32.9 million yuan in 1995 on better management, while turnover dropped 0.2 percent.

Turnover for the petrochemical company, which listed 66 million A shares in Shenzhen last October, dipped slightly to 739.8 million yuan in 1996 compared with 741.2 million yuan, it said in an annual report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange suspended trading of the company's shares on Tuesday morning for the result announcement, and trading resumed in the afternoon, the newspaper said.
Earnings per share reached 0.32 yuan for 1996, up 18.5 percent compared with 0.27 yuan in 1995, it said.
The company attributed its performance to better management and a technological upgrade spurred by its A share listing.
It plans to make a six-for-10 bonus issue from 1996 earnings, to be discussed at a shareholders meeting on April 18, it said in a statement in the newspaper.

Shareholders will also discuss a plan to make a three-for-10 rights issue in 1997 priced at between four and six yuan to raise funds for technological improvement, it said, adding the issue will be based on outstanding shares after the bonus issue.
The company's outstanding shares at the end of 1996 were 147.3 million shares, consisting of 70.5 million state shares, 10.8 million legal persons shares and 66 million A shares.
Main operations of the firm, based in Mudanjiang city in northeastern China's Heilongjiang province, include petrochemical processing.
